rubric_intent: Score a marketing doc for Hyperflow on the depth and credibility of its engineering substance.

dimensions.name: Architecture Specificity
dimensions.description: Measures whether the doc names concrete architectural components, data paths, or system design choices rather than abstract category labels.
dimensions.evidence_instructions: Scan for named subsystems, ingestion/storage/query layers, protocols (OTel, gRPC), runtime details, or deployment topology. Penalize vague phrases like 'cloud-native stack' with no elaboration.

dimensions.name: Quantitative Performance Claims
dimensions.description: Measures presence of concrete numbers (latency, throughput, ingestion rate, cardinality, retention) that characterize the system's behavior.
dimensions.evidence_instructions: Search for figures with units (ms, p99, events/sec, GB, %). Adjectives like 'fast' or 'reliable' without numbers count as absent.

dimensions.name: AI-Workload Domain Depth
dimensions.description: Measures whether the doc demonstrates real understanding of AI/ML observability problems (token usage, prompt/response tracing, eval drift, GPU utilization, model versioning) versus generic observability framing.
dimensions.evidence_instructions: Look for AI-specific concepts: tokens, embeddings, traces of LLM calls, hallucination/eval metrics, GPU/accelerator telemetry, RAG pipelines. Generic 'model performance' counts as shallow.

dimensions.name: Mechanism of Cost & Reliability Claims
dimensions.description: Measures whether claims about cost savings or reliability are explained mechanistically (how the system achieves them) rather than asserted.
dimensions.evidence_instructions: For each cost/reliability claim, check whether the doc describes the underlying mechanism (sampling, tiered storage, anomaly detection, retry logic). Bare assertions score low.

dimensions.name: Integration & Interface Concreteness
dimensions.description: Measures specificity about how engineers actually integrate (SDKs, languages, OTel compatibility, frameworks like LangChain/LlamaIndex, query API).
dimensions.evidence_instructions: Look for named SDKs, supported languages/frameworks, sample code, API endpoints, or instrumentation libraries. Absence of any integration detail scores low.

dimensions.name: Evidence & Verifiability
dimensions.description: Measures whether assertions are backed by verifiable artifacts (benchmarks, case studies with named customers, docs links, postmortems) versus unsupported claims.
dimensions.evidence_instructions: Identify claims like 'trusted by leading AI-first companies' and check for named customers, logos, benchmark methodology, or links. Anonymous social proof scores low.

dimensions.name: Differentiation Substance
dimensions.description: Measures whether the doc explains what makes Hyperflow technically different from alternatives (Datadog, Arize, LangSmith, Honeycomb) at an engineering level.
dimensions.evidence_instructions: Look for comparisons, named alternatives, or specific capabilities competitors lack. Pure superlatives ('next-generation') without contrast score low.

dimensions.name: Buzzword-to-Substance Ratio
dimensions.description: Measures the density of unbacked marketing terms ('next-generation', 'cloud-native', 'instant', 'trusted') relative to substantive technical content.
dimensions.evidence_instructions: Count buzzwords and compare against count of concrete technical nouns/numbers. High buzzword ratio with low substance scores low; technical terms used precisely score high.
